end.summary:
Named liquid, solid ice, and invisible water vapour.
Gave examples from food, rivers, mountains, and air.
Explained that wet clothes dry when water moves into the air due to heat.
Did not yet establish that almost all Earth’s water is salty and only a tiny part is usable fresh water.
Estimated the usable fresh-water share too high.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the three forms of water using familiar examples and guided Sana to connect drying clothes with heat and invisible water vapour. Sana correctly identified the forms and where they are found; the steam-versus-invisible-vapour mix-up was clarified later in the lesson (correctAfterLastSeen: true). The salty-water and tiny-fresh-water idea was not yet secure by the end, so at home, compare a large glass labelled “sea water” with a very small cup labelled “usable fresh water.”
